rationale: C08 is the strongest template because the child expressly reconvenes a Board of Inquiry established on July 6, 1954, and C08 created such a board for the Union Carbide atomic-energy labor dispute. Its continuation clause anticipates precisely the later action: the Board remains in existence to perform other functions required under the Act. C16 corroborates the connection by describing the same C08 dispute and the August 11 injunction that the child specifically references, but it is an intervening injunction-direction letter rather than the instrument establishing the reconvened board. C02 contains nearly identical continuation machinery and has the same date, but concerns a different group of represented employees and is less closely tied to C16's injunction proceedings.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Pursuant to Section 209 (b) of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, you are hereby reconvened as the Board of Inquiry established under [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] dated July 6, 1954
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act.
shared_material.explanation: The child reactivates the particular statutory Board of Inquiry created by C08.

shared_material.child_excerpt: for the purpose of performing such further functions as may be required of you under the said Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, closely shared operative language: C08's continuation provision supplies the mechanism and wording for reconvening the board.

shared_material.child_excerpt: on August 11, 1954, the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee issued an injunction
shared_material.parent_excerpt: at certain facilities of the Atomic Energy Commission located in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and Paducah, Kentucky
shared_material.explanation: The atomic-energy facilities and Tennessee setting align with the dispute for which C08 established the board; C16 independently connects that dispute to the August 11 injunction stage.
